This pinned, single-threaded libjxl decoder reconstructs the **original JPEG bitstream** from JPEG XL's JPEG reconstruction metadata. It does not produce a replacement image rendition. Fidelity continues to display the original JPEG bytes, dimensions, metadata and MIME type. Original scientific sources, credits and terms remain separate from these software licences.

`manifest.json` records source/submodule/compiler pins and hashes. `reconstruct.c` exposes only bounded JPEG reconstruction, requiring the full original output length and consumed input. `decoder.mjs` is unmodified Emscripten output. `decoder-wasm.js` carries the exact WASM bytes as base64 so the full application's existing lossless envelope embeds it without network dependencies. The caller supplies `wasmBinary` and a data-URL location to support the standalone's Blob module import.

The executed build recipe and native/Node/browser exact-byte assessment are recorded in `docs/research/standalone-jxl-reconstruction-assessment-2026-10-19.json`. To rebuild in a new disposable directory, use `scripts/build-jpeg-reconstruction-decoder.sh` with the pinned installed emsdk. The script does not replace vendored output automatically. Compare the resulting WASM hash and run `tests/jpeg-reconstruction.test.js` before updating it. Complete software notices in `NOTICE.txt` are embedded verbatim (with HTML escaping) in the full HTML.

Ordinary builds use the source-hash keyed reconstruction cache and need no native JPEG XL tool. To add entries, run `scripts/generate-jpeg-reconstruction-cache.mjs` with the pinned cjxl/djxl0.11.1 CLI. Both native and WASM reconstruction must match the input bytes before an entry is written. Uncached JPEGs and all other asset formats remain raw. No source asset is resized, re-encoded, removed or replaced.
